subject: Post-discovery: model fit, safety evals, and next steps
messages:
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Katie Lin <katie@healthsync.ai>, Dr. Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@healthsync.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Subject: Post-discovery: model fit, safety evals, and next steps

Hi Katie / Aaron,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the clear run-through of HealthSync's use cases (triage summarization, patient message routing, and clinician-facing decision support). I captured the core constraints we discussed and a recommended plan below so we have a single source of truth.

Summary of constraints we heard
- High safety bar for any consumer-facing clinical suggestions (must refuse when uncertain).
- PHI in prompts and outputs; customer needs encryption-in-transit + audit logs.
- Latency target: median reply < 200ms for short generation paths (triage label + routing).
- Cost sensitivity for high-volume message processing (nightly batch + real-time mix).

Initial model-fit recommendation
- Candidate models: open LLM family (13B class) for a balance of cost & safety: Llama2-13B-QLoRA (if you want SOTA open weights) and Redwood-verified RedM-13B-int8 (our production-tuned variant)
- For safety/abstention-heavy endpoints, we recommend starting with RedM-13B-int8 + a guardrail layer (prompt-level safety templates + a lightweight classifier for refusal triggers).

Evals & benchmarks I will run for you
- Quality regression vs your sample prompt set (we'll use the prompt set you shared + the attached prompt_set_v1)
- Safety/refusal behavior across sensitive scenarios (PHI redaction, medical advice refusal) — we'll run the 'refusal checklist' attachment and collect refusal rates and false refusals
- Latency & cost profile using your throughput assumptions (we'll simulate production burst patterns)

Attachments I shared in this thread
- healthsync_prompt_set_v1.json (your sample prompts + templated variants)
- safety_refusal_checklist.xlsx (initial set of refusal probes we'll run)
- redwood_benchmark_snapshot_mar2026.pdf (example benchmark format / what you'll get)

Next steps / asks (proposed)
1) Confirm data sharing: can you confirm the subset of sample prompts we can ingest for benching (privacy-safe subset preferred)? Ideally a 2k example subset.
2) Approve NDA addendum for test data (I can have legal send a simple one if you want).
3) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive next week with your MLEs; proposed slots Tue/Wed 9–11 PT.
4) We'll deliver an initial eval report (safety + quality + perf) in ~5 business days after we receive the samples.

Quick note on guardrails: we can wire a small policy layer to intercept and return a refusal template when the model confidence metric + classifier threshold indicate risk. We'll include sample refusal templates you can customize.

Open questions for you
- Which of the three endpoints is top priority (triage, routing, decision support)?
- Are you able to share a non-PII sample set for the first pass?

I'll kick off internal scheduling once you confirm the data share path.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0112
https://redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-discovery: model fit, safety evals, and next steps

Rohan —

Thanks for the concise recap. This aligns with our internal notes. A few quick clarifications: 

1) Priority endpoint: triage summarization (we want the lowest risk first). Routing is next. Decision support would be scoped later after we validate abstention behavior.
2) Data share: we can provide a 1.5k-sample non-PII set (we'll scrub PHI fields) by tomorrow EOD. Is that sufficient?
3) Guardrails/custom rules: can Redwood support adding custom refusal triggers (e.g., if prompt contains certain medication names or mentions of self-harm)? We need both out-of-the-box and custom rule support.

Also: can you give an estimate of expected median latency for RedM-13B-int8 in dedicated mode (assuming a standard p3-like GPU)? We're trying to map to our SLA table.

Appreciate the attachments — I'll circulate them internally and confirm the sample set.

Thanks,
Katie
Head of Product | HealthSync
katie@healthsync.ai

Katie — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming priority = triage. Short answers to your questions + a couple concrete numbers so you can slot into your SLA table.

Guardrails / custom rules
- Yes, we support both: 1) prompt-level safety templates you control (e.g., include a "must_refuse_on" list) and 2) a rule engine for custom triggers (exact-match drug lists, regexes for self-harm, patient id patterns). We can bundle policies as JSON so your engineering team can version them.

Latency estimates (RedM-13B-int8)
- Hosted / Dedicated (single-GPU p3-equivalent): median 120–180ms for 32-token outputs with continuous batching off.
- With our autoscaling / batching for high-throughput, p50 can increase slightly depending on batch profile; we'll provide a simulated latency curve in the benchmark report.

Eval plan & timeline
- Once we receive the scrubbed 1.5k prompts (thanks — that's perfect), we'll: 
  a) Run the prompt set against RedM-13B-int8 and Llama2-13B-QLoRA
  b) Execute the safety_refusal_checklist across crafted probes (we'll flag false negatives/false positives)
  c) Deliver an initial report with: quality metrics (exact match / BLEU-like proxies where useful), refusal rate, example failure cases, latency/cost table.

Deliverables
- HealthSync Eval Report (PDF)
- CSV of flagged examples + model outputs (for your review)
- Guardrail JSON template and recommended thresholds

Proposed meeting slots
- Tue 17 Mar, 09:00–10:00 PT (technical deep-dive)
- Wed 18 Mar, 10:00–11:00 PT (alternate)

If either of those work, I'll send a calendar invite and include Ben (solutions engineer) for the demo piece.

Best,
Rohan
